Both work. This version has a few more example bookmarks so filtering is meaningful. The **search box behaves the same in both** — it's the **tag filtering** that differs.

**First, try search (same in both).** Open http://maker:4001/filter.html?mode=f1 and type `solnit` (or `grid`, or `slow`) in the search box. It matches across the **title, description, note, and tags**, and highlights the hit. Clear it when done.

**Now compare the two ways to filter by tag:**

**Version F1 — a tag filter bar:** stay on http://maker:4001/filter.html?mode=f1
Under the search box there's a **"Filter by tag:"** row of all your tags. Click **`dev`** — the list narrows to dev bookmarks. Notice you can also **type in search at the same time** to combine them. Click `dev` again to clear.

**Version F2 — click a tag on a card:** open http://maker:4001/filter.html?mode=f2
There's no filter bar. Instead, on any bookmark, **click one of its tag chips** — e.g. click **`reading`** on an item. It filters to that tag, and a **"Showing tag …"** note with a **clear** link appears at the top.

The trade-off: **F1** shows you all your tags up front (easy to browse what you have), while **F2** keeps the screen cleaner and you filter from whatever you happen to be looking at.

Which way of narrowing down by tag feels more natural to you? And does the search box — matching title, description, note, and tags together — cover how you'd expect to "find" something?
